item.text:
**Verdict**  
Mixed, leaning **no**. Sharif’s 2024 record contains real welfare-oriented policy elements, but most strong positives are IMF/World Bank programmatic commitments or reactive fixes, while the broader state practice still showed coercion, exclusion, and weak protection for vulnerable groups.

**Positive Evidence**
- **Pakistan: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on Economic Policies with Pakistan for 37-month Extended Fund Facility** | IMF | 2024-07-12 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff  
  The IMF said the program aimed to create stronger, more inclusive, resilient growth, explicitly expanding BISP social protection and increasing education and health spending. This is the clearest evidence that welfare was treated as a real policy objective, not only as rhetoric. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9, 5B.3

- **Pakistan: World Bank Approves $535 Million for Crisis-Resilient Social Protection and Climate-Smart Growth in the Livestock and Aquaculture Sectors** | World Bank | 2024-06-20 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/20/pakistan-world-bank-approves-535-million-for-crisis-resilient-social-protection-and-climate-smart-growth-in-the-livestoc  
  The World Bank said Pakistan was strengthening its social protection system to help poor and vulnerable households absorb climate and economic shocks, and noted support for female farmers and food security. This supports a welfare-first reading, though it is institutional finance rather than proof of Sharif personally prioritizing welfare. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9, 5B.10

- **World Report 2024: Pakistan** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/pakistan  
  HRW noted that after its reporting on prison health, Sharif ordered sanitation and health-care measures in Lahore Central Prison and vowed prison reforms nationwide. This is a concrete welfare-related intervention, though it was reactive and narrow. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.9, 5B.8

- **National Minorities Day being observed today** | Radio Pakistan | 2024-08-11 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/11-08-2024/national-minorities-day-being-observed  
  State media framed National Minorities Day around religious and socio-economic rights and equal citizenship. This is positive public welfare/equality language, though still largely rhetorical. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8

- **Government of Pakistan, human-rights measures** | Press Information Department | 2024-12-10 | https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/27376  
  The government said it had taken legislative steps for vulnerable groups, cited commissions for women, children, and human rights, and said the minorities commission had been strengthened. This is the best institutional evidence of a welfare-and-rights framing. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8

**Negative Evidence**
- **Pakistan: Widening Crackdown on Dissent** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent  
  HRW said the government clamped down on media, opposition, and NGOs, and that failure to ensure adequate social security jeopardized rights to health, food, and an adequate standard of living. That cuts against treating human welfare as the core purpose of rule. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Pakistan: Authorities must end escalating attacks on minority Ahmadiyya community** | Amnesty International | 2024-06-21 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/  
  Amnesty documented arbitrary arrests, police harassment, and blocked religious rites for Ahmadis, while authorities failed to ensure safety. This is strong evidence that vulnerable-group welfare was not a governing priority in practice. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Pakistan: The new Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act threatens the right to protest** | Amnesty International | 2024-09-09 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/  
  Amnesty said the government rushed through draconian protest restrictions instead of aligning rules with human-rights standards. That suggests state authority and regime control were often prioritized over civic welfare and dignity. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Pakistan: Urgent and transparent investigation needed into deadly crackdown on opposition protesters** | Amnesty International | 2024-11-27 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/urgent-and-transparent-investigation-needed-into-deadly-crackdown-on-opposition-protesters/  
  Amnesty described deaths, mass detentions, and a communications blackout during the Islamabad crackdown. That is direct counterevidence to a welfare-centered conception of rule. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Pakistan: Abusive Evictions Target Urban Poor** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-28 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/28/pakistan-abusive-evictions-target-urban-poor  
  HRW reported forcible evictions of low-income residents, shop owners, and street vendors without adequate notice, compensation, or resettlement. This strongly suggests that the state was not treating the welfare of the poor as a core governing purpose. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8

- **HRCP general body calls for consensus on civilian autonomy, climate justice and land rights** | Human Rights Commission of Pakistan | 2024-11-17 | https://hrcp.wittywebsolutions.com/hrcp-general-body-calls-for-consensus-on-civilian-autonomy-climate-justice-and-land-rights-2/  
  HRCP said the state should focus on health, education, workers, peasants, and women and instead had prioritized authority over rights. This is a strong domestic civil-society judgment against a welfare-first state. IDs: 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

**Search Gap**
- I found stronger evidence for **policy language and institutional programs** than for durable, independently measured welfare outcomes.
- I did **not** find a 2024 source proving that Sharif personally made human welfare the overriding purpose of rule across the board.
- The best pro-welfare evidence is mostly IMF/World Bank program design, minority-rights messaging, and one prison-reform intervention, while the strongest counterevidence comes from repression, evictions, and unequal treatment of vulnerable groups.
